record.paper_title: Ultra-Dense Cell-Free Massive MIMO for 6G: Technical Overview and Open Questions
record.original_question: What role should uplink and downlink power control play in scalable cell-free massive multiple-input multiple-output (CF-MMIMO), and how can power-control methods balance sum spectral efficiency, fairness, near-far mitigation, interference control, centralization versus distribution, partial channel state information (CSI) sharing, and the practical limits of machine-learning or reinforcement-learning approaches?

evidence.quote: G. What is the Role of Power Control?
As in any wireless network, power allocation is important in CF-MMIMO to tackle the near-far effect and minimize the interference [14], [52].
Any non-trivial network-wide optimal power allocation is unscalable as the number of AP and/or users grows unboundedly.

To summarize, to preserve the scalability of the system, power control implementations should be either heuristic and fully distributed, or sub-optimal and centralized but requiring only partial CSI sharing.
Such techniques are thus unscalable and impractical.

artifact.category_tag: Scalable power control in cell-free massive MIMO
artifact.status_search_result: Scalable uplink/downlink power control in cell-free massive MIMO is an active and unresolved research area. Recent works (2023–2025) propose distributed heuristics, deep-learning, and reinforcement-learning approaches with partial CSI, but no scheme has been shown to fully reconcile sum-SE, fairness, near-far mitigation, and scalability with provable optimality guarantees, so the broad question remains open.
